content: CCDC137, also known as Coiled-coil domain containing 137, is a protein encoded by the CCDC137 gene in humans. To investigate the function of CCDC137, model organisms have been utilized. Specifically, a conditional knockout mouse line named Ccdc137tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi was created as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This program is a large-scale mutagenesis initiative aimed at generating and distributing animal models of human diseases to researchers worldwide. The mouse line was developed at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute. Both male and female mice from this knockout line underwent a standardized phenotypic screening process to assess the consequences of the gene deletion. A total of 25 different tests were conducted on the mutant mice. Among these, two significant abnormalities were identified. Notably, no homozygous mutant embryos were detected during gestation, and in a separate study, no homozygous mutant animals were observed at the weaning stage. The remaining tests were performed on adult heterozygous mutant mice. However, no additional abnormalities were identified in these animals.
